text:
maya: Heads-up — onboarding argo-52k-int3 (int3 quant) and seeing prefills blow up when we cross ~50k tokens. Small repro attached.
zoe: ugh. is this the warm-prefill vs in-flight mismatch again?
maya: Possibly. Repro: single prompt ~52k tokens, then continue generating. After ~50k, answers start hallucinating previously primed context (ghost tokens).
liam: can you paste the snippet of the kv index mismatch?
maya: sure — here's the short log from runtime when repair triggered:
```
[kv] shard=3 prefill_len=51996 primed_keys=51996
[kv] index_map[51995]=51994
[kv] index_map[51996]=0  <-- wrap?
[kv] generation_offset=51996
```
zoe: index_map[51996]=0 looks like a fencepost wrap. maybe the rot_pos packing overflowed.
rafael: which rotary scheme is argo using? phase-scaling or classic RoPE?
maya: phase-scaling enabled (pos_scale=1.0, dyn_rescale=false). Works fine at 48k, fails at ~50k.
jen: did you try flipping pos_scale slightly >1 to see if it shifts the boundary?
maya: tried pos_scale=1.0001 — pushed the failure to ~50,040. So it's an off-by-one at a window boundary rather than pure scale.
liam: sounds like a prefill shard boundary where our KV circular buffer size calculation uses block_size * shard_count but there's an off-by-one if token_count % block_size == 0.
zoe: can we run a quick instrumented run with extra assertions in kv_write to catch wrap events?
maya: running now on canary (quant-run-112). command: `INSTRUMENT_KV=1 make run-model MODEL=argo-52k-int3 SEED=42`
ops-bot: Deploy started: canary/quant-run-112 by maya at 2026-03-23T14:12:03Z
rafael: also check memcpy padding — int3 layout changed the stride, could cause index miscalc in compacted buffer.
jen: good call. int3 packer does 5bits/word, we had a bug where tail stride used (bytes_per_row-1) in a couple places.
liam: if it's padding, it would show as occasional dropped keys, not continuous wrap. but both hypotheses plausible.
zoe: maya, can you grab the payload that triggers the repro and put it in /tmp/argo-repro-6242.json? I'll run a low-latency tracer.
maya: uploaded to s3: s3://redwood-repro/argo/6242424242/payload.json
zoe: starting tracer on node 7. will livestream logs shortly.
ops-bot: Trace session 772 attached to canary/quant-run-112
zoe: early logs show kv_write at token 51996 doing a memcopy of size 0x1e00 to offset 0x0. suspicious.
rafael: offset 0x0 from a nonzero token — that matches an accidental modulus collapse. probably an integer cast in the indexing code.
jen: i can push a quick fix to quant4-packer branch to clamp the index math and add assert(token_index < buffer_len). want me to PR?
maya: please do. If we add an assert, we should gate behind build flag to avoid customer regressions.
liam: also let's add a metric for "kv_wrap_events" (increment when index_map[x] < index_map[x-1]) so we can signal in telemetry.
zoe: agree. Telemetry would have caught previous runs earlier.
rafael: backlog note: run full regression on magnet and argo families after PR. prioritise argo-52k-int3.
jen: PR posted: https://github.com/redwood/serving/pull/9654 — adds clamp + telemetry + unit test for buffer boundary.
maya: pulled and built canary image, re-running repro. will post results.
ops-bot: Build success: image redwood/serving:canary-9654 (sha: ab12ef)
maya: quick update — with clamp and assertion off, repro still happens but now we log wrap events. Got 3 wraps at tokens: 51996, 52000, 52008.
liam: multiple wraps means the underlying calc oscillates — maybe a race between prefill and streaming writes where prefill reserves N tokens but streaming shifts the base.
zoe: are we running with continuous batching? Batching might coalesce writes across shards and cause reindexing races.
maya: yes continuous batching enabled in canary. disabling it temporarily eliminates the repro (ran once).
rafael: that points to ordering/race in the batching coalescer. possibly when a batch flush overlaps with KV prefill flush we do a second modulus calc against an already advanced head.
jen: proposed mitigation: make KV reserve + write atomic via a small lock or change ring semantics to use sequence numbers (seq++) and compute offsets from seq_base. of course locks degrade throughput.
liam: maybe use per-shard sequence numbers (lightweight) and avoid global locks. sequence arithmetic should be cheap.
zoe: short-term: disable continuous batching for argo-52k-int3 in dedicated canaries until we fix. long-term: change to seq-based offsets + telemetry.
maya: agreeing. I'll open an infra change to flip batching off for that model family.
jen: also we should add a fuzzbench for longprefill sequences crossing boundaries; current test matrix stops at 48k. add cases at 51k, 52k, 65k.
rafael: will coordinate with QA.
maya: TL;DR: root cause likely batching/coalescing race with int3 packing + ring index calc off-by-one. Mitigation: disable continuous batching for affected model, PR landed with clamps/telemetry, follow-up change to seq-based indexing.
liam: thx for the triage. ping me when infra flip is live and I'll run full regression.
zoe: noted and added to oncall playbook under "prefill-wrap". :white_check_mark:
maya: thanks all. I'll update the canary thread with regression results in ~30m.
